notes: A made-up class (the coins of the Halvard find) under a real one (the 1870-S three-dollar piece, of which only one is known with certainty). Could it exist unrecorded (README, Insert)? Yes: a newly reported find of a rare coin adds to its "known" count without falsifying anything documented. The class (the coins of the find) is made up; the find is not empty, as the word says. A second specimen is even documented as possible: one was reportedly struck for the cornerstone of the San Francisco Mint and its fate is unknown. R2: "1870-S" contains the mint mark; the mint query tests reading it through a firm fact, and no query asks the face value ("three-dollar" names it). Weak point: the 1870-S is rarely mentioned (Dolma), so checks will drop the record for some models. A replaced draft (a new £25 Bank of England note) broke the "could it exist unrecorded" rule.
